qs.q:
Bloggers — Which person…

A=Anna (started at 14, launched magazine 'Prize' at 16, personal style/shopping/fashion blog, ignores trolls, earns advertising)
B=Ben (weightlifter, photographer, world traveller; blends science and biographies; passes on habits for well-being; easy to start)
C=Cate (started at 15, politics blog; trolls doubted teenager could blog on politics; more time on studies now in college)
D=Damon (vegetarian food blog 'Biscuit Bob' with cute dog photos; won award; felt uncomfortable at first; took time to find topic)
E=Ellen (started without plan; film reviews; no readers for ages; then national press noticed; 30,000 hits/month; wants to be director)
F=Frank (longstanding wellness/mindfulness blog; went from depressed/unhealthy to running marathons; advises readers to slow down)

0. began blogging when they were 14? [A=Anna]
1. blogs less than they used to?
2. won an award for their work?
3. had their blog recognised by major newspapers?
4. had a job they didn't like?
5. started a publication?
6. ignores negative feedback?
7. didn't get any attention at first?
8. says it doesn't take long to set up a blog?
9. shares other people's advice in their blog?
10. felt under pressure to change their field of interest?
11. didn't enjoy blogging at the beginning?
12. is planning a change of career?
items: 1 — blogs less than they used to?
2 — won an award for their work?
3 — had their blog recognised by major newspapers?
4 — had a job they didn't like?
7 — didn't get any attention at first?
8 — says it doesn't take long to set up a blog?
9 — shares other people's advice in their blog?
10 — felt under pressure to change their field of interest?
11 — didn't enjoy blogging at the beginning?
12 — is planning a change of career?

qs.q:
The history of infectious diseases

"When an epidemic spreads beyond a country's borders, the disease officially becomes a PANDEMIC."

The writer says that infectious diseases…
A are termed epidemics when they spread abroad.
B are considered worst case scenarios.
C affected hunter-gatherer societies.
D started about 10,000 years ago.
opts: are termed epidemics when they spread abroad.

qs.q:
The history of infectious diseases

"As we became more civilised, built more cities, FORGED TRADE ROUTES to connect with other cities, and of course WAGED WARS, the more likely pandemics became."

According to the second paragraph, the first pandemics…
A were facilitated by cities and trade.
B caused wars in early civilisations.
C killed two thirds of the population.
D helped defeat the Spartans.
opts: were facilitated by cities and trade.
killed two thirds of the population.

qs.q:
The history of infectious diseases

"RETURNING ROMAN TROOPS spread it throughout the Roman Empire."

The Antonine plague…
A was started by Roman soldiers returning to their homes.
B started among German troops fighting the Romans.
C was confirmed as the first outbreak of smallpox.
D infected a Roman Emperor.
opts: was started by Roman soldiers returning to their homes.
started among German troops fighting the Romans.
was confirmed as the first outbreak of smallpox.

qs.q:
The history of infectious diseases

"Leprosy was believed to be A PUNISHMENT FROM GOD that ran in families."

The writer says that leprosy…
A resulted in a focus on pandemics.
B was considered to be a divine penalty.
C kills tens of thousands of people a year.
D first appeared in Europe in the Middle Ages.
opts: resulted in a focus on pandemics.
was considered to be a divine penalty.
kills tens of thousands of people a year.
first appeared in Europe in the Middle Ages.

qs.q:
The history of infectious diseases

"The Black Death entered Europe through Sicily in 1347 AD, when people with the plague ARRIVED IN THE PORT OF MESSINA FROM THE FAR EAST."

According to the fifth paragraph, the Black Death…
A was brought into Europe by travellers.
B spread to North America through the Vikings.
C made England and France go to war with each other.
D was made worse by economic circumstances and demographics.
opts: was brought into Europe by travellers.
spread to North America through the Vikings.
made England and France go to war with each other.
was made worse by economic circumstances and demographics.

qs.q:
The history of infectious diseases

"A combination of smallpox, measles and bubonic plague... IT WEAKENED THE POPULATION so they were unable to RESIST THE SPANISH COLONIZERS."

A combination of smallpox, measles and the bubonic plague…
A were found by Christopher Columbus on the island of Hispaniola.
B infected indigenous people before the Spanish invasion.
C helped the Spanish to conquer the Americas.
D brought down the Aztec Empire in 1520.
opts: were found by Christopher Columbus on the island of Hispaniola.
infected indigenous people before the Spanish invasion.
helped the Spanish to conquer the Americas.
brought down the Aztec Empire in 1520.

qs.q:
Handwriting

"Most people learn to write by reproducing letters from a copybook at a young age. (19) ____. It is based on each writer's perception of the image and his or her ability (motor skills) to reproduce that visual perception."

A A writer's identity cannot be established through a single individual feature.
B Once this occurs, writers focus on the subject matter rather than the physical act of writing.
C However, these studies all found that trained experts were able to distinguish between the handwriting of twins.
D Even identical twins do not have the same handwriting.
E Because handwriting is relatively stable, a change can be indicative of the writer's nervousness.
F This ability to copy the letters varies from one child to the next.
G In contrast, experts can tell the difference between both the obvious features and the less conspicuous elements.
H Instead, the relationship between handwriting and personality has been firmly established.
opts: A — A writer's identity cannot be established through a single feature.
B — Once this occurs, writers focus on the subject matter.
C — However, trained experts were able to distinguish twins' handwriting.
D — Even identical twins do not have the same handwriting.
E — A change in handwriting can be indicative of the writer's nervousness.
F — This ability to copy the letters varies from one child to the next.
G — In contrast, experts can tell the difference between obvious and less conspicuous elements.
H — Instead, the relationship between handwriting and personality has been firmly established.
